items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: Yes, he was a very good friend of the families.

ctx.x: Were there any particular bands or specific musicians who were especially encouraging when you were just trying to get into the jazz or if you will ragtime playing?

Right. There were no specific musicians, Charlie, in the early period because if you will figure this, that I started taking lessons when I was about eight or nine years old. And, of course, that's pretty young, you know, especially when you go back into those old days and people, the way they were, you know, kind of strict, you didn't get much chance to get out too much. Right. I didn't meet too many musicians. I wasn't around too many musicians. But there was one man, his name was Edward Bordeaux. I have never…
Would you remember how you spelled his name, Bordeaux, you said?
